subproblems.title: Gauss–Green measure: Riesz representation of the perimeter functional (Simon Ch. 2, 2.1–2.2; Ch. 3, 4.1)
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, let D ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} be open and F ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} Borel. Assume that for every compact K ⊆ D there is C_K ∈ ℝ with ∫_F div φ dL^{m+1} ≤ C_K for all C^∞ compactly supported φ : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m+1} with tsupport φ ⊆ K and |φ| ≤ 1 (div φ = trace Dφ). Then there are a Borel measure μ on ℝ^{m+1} and a Borel map ν : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m+1} such that μ(ℝ^{m+1} \ D) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ D, |ν(y)| = 1 for every y, and ∫_F div φ dL^{m+1} = −∫⟨φ, ν⟩ dμ for every C¹ compactly supported φ : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m+1} with tsupport φ ⊆ D.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Simon Ch. 2, 2.1–2.2 (chapter-02.txt lines 477–505) and Ch. 3, 4.1 (chapter-03.txt lines 555–575), with the Riesz Representation Theorem Ch. 1, 4.14 (chapter-01.txt line 1654; SimonGMT `simon_theorem_4_14`, `simon_theorem_4_14_caratheodory` in Chapter01/RadonPolarRepresentation.lean). This is steps 1–2 of the parent proof. Erratum: the OCR of 4.1 drops the minus sign; for the inward normal ν the identity reads ∫_F div g = −∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ.

Notation. E := ℝ^{m+1}, L := L^{m+1}, div φ := trace Dφ, ‖g‖_∞ := sup|g|. For compact K and d > 0, K^d := {x : dist(x, K) ≤ d} (compact). As D is open, every compact K ⊆ D has some d_K > 0 with K^{2d_K} ⊆ D.

1. Two-sided bound. Fix a compact K ⊆ D and C_K from the hypothesis. φ = 0 is admissible, so C_K ≥ 0. If φ is C^∞, compactly supported, tsupport φ ⊆ K and φ ≠ 0, then ±φ/‖φ‖_∞ are admissible and div is linear, so |∫_F div φ dL| ≤ C_K ‖φ‖_∞; this also holds for φ = 0. (div φ is continuous with compact support, hence L-integrable on F.)

2. Mollification. Fix ρ ∈ C_c^∞(E) with ρ ≥ 0, ∫ρ = 1, spt ρ ⊆ B_1(0) (Mathlib `ContDiffBump.normed` for a bump centred at 0 with outer radius 1), and ρ_ε(x) := ε^{-(m+1)} ρ(x/ε). For g : E → E continuous with compact support put g_ε := ρ_ε * g (componentwise). Then g_ε is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left); tsupport g_ε ⊆ (tsupport g)^ε; |g_ε(x)| ≤ ∫ρ_ε(x − z)|g(z)| dz ≤ ‖g‖_∞; and g_ε → g uniformly as ε ↓ 0 (g is uniformly continuous). If g is C¹, then D(g_ε) = ρ_ε * Dg, hence div g_ε = ρ_ε * div g → div g uniformly.

3. Extension. Let 𝒞 := {g : E → E continuous, compactly supported, tsupport g ⊆ D}. For g ∈ 𝒞, K := tsupport g and 0 < ε, ε′ < d_K, the field g_ε − g_{ε′} is C^∞ with tsupport in K^{d_K}, so by step 1 |∫_F div g_ε − ∫_F div g_{ε′}| ≤ C_{K^{d_K}} ‖g_ε − g_{ε′}‖_∞ → 0. Hence Λ(g) := −lim_{ε↓0} ∫_F div g_ε dL exists. Properties:
 (a) Λ is linear on 𝒞 (for g, h ∈ 𝒞 use the compact set tsupport g ∪ tsupport h; (g + h)_ε = g_ε + h_ε and (cg)_ε = c g_ε).
 (b) If g ∈ 𝒞 is C¹ then Λ(g) = −∫_F div g dL: div g_ε → div g uniformly and all these functions vanish outside the compact set K^{d_K}, of finite L-measure.
 (c) Local bound: if K ⊆ D is compact, g ∈ 𝒞, tsupport g ⊆ K and |g| ≤ 1, then |g_ε| ≤ 1 and tsupport g_ε ⊆ K^{d_K} for ε < d_K, so |Λ(g)| ≤ C_{K^{d_K}}.

4. Riesz representation on D. Regard D (an open subspace of E) as a locally compact Hausdorff space. For h ∈ C_c(D; E) its extension by zero h̃ lies in 𝒞: h̃ is continuous on the open set D and vanishes on the open set E \ tsupport_D h (a compact subset of D is closed in E), and these open sets cover E. Define L(h) := Λ(h̃); it is linear by 3(a), and for every compact K ⊆ D, L(h) ≤ C_{K^{d_K}} whenever |h| ≤ 1 and supp h ⊆ K, by 3(c). By Simon Ch. 1, 4.14 (X = D, H = E; SimonGMT `simon_theorem_4_14_caratheodory`) there are a Radon measure μ_D on D and a μ_D-measurable ν_D : D → E with |ν_D| = 1 μ_D-a.e. and L(h) = ∫_D ⟨h, ν_D⟩ dμ_D for all h ∈ C_c(D; E).

5. Transfer to E. Define the Borel measure μ(A) := μ_D(A ∩ D): the Borel restriction of the Carathéodory measure of μ_D (SimonGMT `opensMeasurableSpace_radonCaratheodoryMeasure`, `IsBorelRegularOuterMeasure.toBorelMeasure`) pushed forward along the inclusion D ↪ E. Then μ(E \ D) = 0 and μ(K) = μ_D(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ D. The Riesz field ν_D is measurable for the Carathéodory σ-algebra of μ_D; as μ_D is Borel regular and open σ-finite (D is σ-compact and μ_D is finite on compacts), each coordinate of ν_D is μ_D-a.e. equal to a Borel function (SimonGMT `IsBorelRegularOuterMeasure.aemeasurable_of_caratheodory`, applied coordinatewise; E is finite-dimensional). Hence ν_D agrees μ_D-a.e. with a Borel map ν₁ : E → E (on D), and integrals against the Carathéodory measure of μ_D and against μ coincide for such integrands. Fix a unit vector e ∈ E (E ≠ {0}) and set ν(y) := ν₁(y) if |ν₁(y)| = 1, ν(y) := e otherwise. Then ν is Borel, |ν(y)| = 1 for every y, and ν = ν_D μ-a.e. on D. Hence for g ∈ 𝒞: Λ(g) = L(g|_D) = ∫_D ⟨g, ν_D⟩ dμ_D = ∫_E ⟨g, ν⟩ dμ (the integrand is bounded and vanishes off the compact set tsupport g ⊆ D, which has finite μ-measure, so it is μ-integrable).

6. Gauss–Green. Let φ be C¹ with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ D. Then φ ∈ 𝒞, and by 3(b) and step 5, −∫_F div φ dL = Λ(φ) = ∫⟨φ, ν⟩ dμ. With step 5 this gives every assertion: μ(E \ D) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ D, ν Borel with |ν| ≡ 1, and ∫_F div φ dL = −∫⟨φ, ν⟩ dμ. ∎
proof_key_steps: Hypothesis applied to ±φ/sup|φ| gives |∫_F div φ| ≤ C_K sup|φ| for smooth φ supported in K.
Mollification gives smooth approximants supported in K^d with sup bound preserved and uniformly convergent divergence for C¹ fields.
Λ := −lim ∫_F div g_ε is a locally bounded linear functional on continuous compactly supported fields in D and equals −∫_F div g on C¹ fields.
Simon Ch. 1, 4.14 on the locally compact space D yields a Radon μ_D and a unit polar field ν_D.
Push μ_D forward to ℝ^{m+1}; take a Borel representative of ν_D and make it unit everywhere.
Gauss–Green identity for C¹ fields from 3(b) and the representation.

subproblems.title: Reduced boundary has full measure: differentiation of the normal (Simon Ch. 3, 4.2; Ch. 1, 3.23)
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, let D ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} be open, let μ be a Borel measure on ℝ^{m+1} with μ(ℝ^{m+1} \ D) = 0 and μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ D, and let ν : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m+1} be Borel with |ν(y)| = 1 for every y. Then for μ-a.e. y: y ∈ D and μ(B̄_ρ(y))_ℝ^{-1} ∫_{B̄_ρ(y)} ν dμ → ν(y) as ρ ↓ 0 (μ(·)_ℝ = ENNReal.toReal, 0^{-1} = 0).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Simon Ch. 3, (4.2) and the sentence after it (chapter-03.txt lines 580–586: "by virtue of Theorem 3.23 of Ch. 1 we have μ_E(U \ ∂*E) = 0"), using the differentiation theorem Ch. 1, 3.23 (chapter-01.txt line 1063); parent proof step 3. In Mathlib this is Lebesgue–Besicovitch differentiation for the Besicovitch Vitali family of closed balls (Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Covering/Besicovitch.lean, Differentiation.lean).

Notation. E := ℝ^{m+1}; A_μ(y, ρ) := μ(B̄_ρ(y))_ℝ^{-1} ∫_{B̄_ρ(y)} ν dμ.

1. μ-a.e. point lies in D, because μ(E \ D) = 0.

2. Exhaustion. If D = ∅ there is nothing more to prove. For j ≥ 1 let K_j := {x ∈ E : |x| ≤ j and dist(x, E \ D) ≥ 1/j} (K_j := {|x| ≤ j} if D = E). Each K_j is compact, K_j ⊆ D, and every y ∈ D lies in the interior of some K_j (choose j with |y| < j and dist(y, E \ D) > 1/j). Let μ_j := μ⌞K_j, a finite (hence locally finite) Borel measure since μ(K_j) < ∞.

3. Differentiation for μ_j. ν is bounded and Borel, hence μ_j-integrable. By Lebesgue–Besicovitch differentiation (Mathlib `VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average` for `Besicovitch.vitaliFamily μ_j`, combined with `Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt` to pass from the Vitali filter to the closed balls B̄_ρ(y), ρ ↓ 0) there is a μ_j-null set N_j such that A_{μ_j}(y, ρ) → ν(y) as ρ ↓ 0 for every y ∉ N_j.

4. Localization. Let y ∈ int K_j \ N_j and 0 < ρ < dist(y, E \ K_j). Then B̄_ρ(y) ⊆ K_j, so μ_j(B̄_ρ(y)) = μ(B̄_ρ(y)) and ∫_{B̄_ρ(y)} ν dμ_j = ∫_{B̄_ρ(y)} ν dμ. Hence A_μ(y, ρ) = A_{μ_j}(y, ρ) for all small ρ, and A_μ(y, ρ) → ν(y). Moreover μ(N_j ∩ K_j) = μ_j(N_j) = 0.

5. Conclusion. If y ∈ D and A_μ(y, ρ) does not converge to ν(y), then y ∈ N_j ∩ K_j for any j with y ∈ int K_j. So the exceptional set is contained in (E \ D) ∪ ⋃_j (N_j ∩ K_j), a countable union of μ-null sets. Hence for μ-a.e. y: y ∈ D and A_μ(y, ρ) → ν(y) as ρ ↓ 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: μ-a.e. point lies in D.
Exhaust D by compacts K_j with D = ⋃ int K_j; μ⌞K_j is finite.
Besicovitch differentiation of the bounded Borel field ν for μ⌞K_j over closed balls.
Near interior points of K_j the averages for μ and μ⌞K_j coincide.
Countable union of null exceptional sets.

subproblems.title: Cut-off estimates at a reduced-boundary point: annular bounds and upper density (De Giorgi; Simon 4.3 (1), (3)–(6))
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ. Suppose D ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} is open, F ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} is Borel, μ is a Borel measure on ℝ^{m+1} with μ(ℝ^{m+1} \ D) = 0 and μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ D, ν : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m+1} is Borel with |ν(z)| = 1 for every z, and the Gauss–Green identity (GG) ∫_F div φ dL^{m+1} = −∫⟨φ, ν⟩ dμ holds for every C¹ compactly supported φ : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m+1} with tsupport φ ⊆ D (div φ = trace Dφ, L^{m+1} = volume). Let y ∈ D and v ∈ ℝ^{m+1} with |v| = 1 be such that the normal averages A(ρ) := μ(B̄_ρ(y))_ℝ^{-1} ∫_{B̄_ρ(y)} ν dμ converge to v as ρ ↓ 0 (μ(·)_ℝ = ENNReal.toReal, 0^{-1} = 0). Then there are ρ₁ > 0 and C ≥ 0 with B̄_{ρ₁}(y) ⊆ D such that for all ρ, δ > 0 with ρ + δ < ρ₁: δ·μ(B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ C·L^{m+1}(F ∩ (B_{ρ+δ}(y) \ B̄_ρ(y))) and δ·μ(B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ C·L^{m+1}((B_{ρ+δ}(y) \ B̄_ρ(y)) \ F); and μ(B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ C ρ^m for all 0 < ρ < ρ₁.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Printed proof of Simon Ch. 3, 4.3, steps (1) and (3)–(6) (chapter-03.txt lines 604–652); parent proof step 4 (1)–(6). Departures, made only so that the C¹ Gauss–Green identity suffices and no derivative of ρ ↦ L(F ∩ B_ρ) is needed: Simon's Lipschitz cut-offs decreasing to 1_{B̄_ρ} and the derivative in (4)–(6) are replaced by one C¹ cut-off per pair (ρ, δ) and a layer-cake (Fubini) argument, giving finite-difference forms of (5)–(6); the constant 2 in (6) becomes 3.

Notation. E := ℝ^{m+1}, L := L^{m+1}, B_r := B_r(y), B̄_r := B̄_r(y), A(r) := μ(B̄_r)_ℝ^{-1} ∫_{B̄_r} ν dμ, ω_{m+1} := L(B_1(0)).

1. Radii. As D is open, fix ρ₀ > 0 with B̄_{ρ₀} ⊆ D; then μ(B̄_r) ≤ μ(B̄_{ρ₀}) < ∞ for r ≤ ρ₀. Since ⟨A(r), v⟩ → |v|² = 1, choose ρ₂ ∈ (0, ρ₀] with ⟨A(r), v⟩ ≥ 1/2 for 0 < r < ρ₂. For such r, A(r) ≠ 0, so 0 < μ(B̄_r) < ∞ and (quantitative printed (1))
 (1′) ∫_{B̄_r} ⟨ν, v⟩ dμ = μ(B̄_r)⟨A(r), v⟩ ≥ ½ μ(B̄_r) for 0 < r < ρ₂.
 Put ρ₁ := ρ₂/2.

2. Cut-off. Let h(t) := 1 for t ≤ 0, h(t) := 1 − 3t² + 2t³ for 0 ≤ t ≤ 1, h(t) := 0 for t ≥ 1. h is C¹, nonincreasing, strictly decreasing on [0, 1], h′(0) = h′(1) = 0 and |h′| ≤ 3/2. For ρ, δ > 0 with ρ + δ < ρ₂ let ζ(z) := h((|z − y| − ρ)/δ). ζ ≡ 1 on the open ball B_ρ, a neighbourhood of y, and on E \ {y} it is a composition of C¹ maps; hence ζ is C¹ on E. Moreover 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1, ζ = 1 on B̄_ρ, tsupport ζ ⊆ B̄_{ρ+δ} ⊆ D, and ∇ζ(z) = δ^{-1} h′((|z − y| − ρ)/δ)(z − y)/|z − y| vanishes unless ρ < |z − y| < ρ + δ, with |∇ζ| ≤ 3/(2δ).

3. Gauss–Green (printed (3)–(5)). φ := ζ v is C¹, compactly supported, tsupport φ ⊆ D, and div φ = ⟨∇ζ, v⟩. By (GG),
 ∫ ζ ⟨ν, v⟩ dμ = −∫_F ⟨∇ζ, v⟩ dL ≤ ∫_F |∇ζ| dL ≤ (3/(2δ)) L(F ∩ (B_{ρ+δ} \ B̄_ρ)).

4. Layer cake. For every z, ζ(z) = ∫_0^1 1{ζ(z) ≥ t} dt, and for t ∈ (0, 1], {ζ ≥ t} = B̄_{r(t)} with r(t) := ρ + δ s(t) ∈ [ρ, ρ + δ), where s(t) := max{s ∈ [0, 1] : h(s) ≥ t} (h is continuous and nonincreasing). The function (t, z) ↦ 1{ζ(z) ≥ t}⟨ν(z), v⟩ is Borel and bounded by 1_{B̄_{ρ+δ}}(z), which is integrable for dt ⊗ μ on (0, 1) × E. By Fubini and (1′) (note r(t) < ρ₂),
 ∫ ζ ⟨ν, v⟩ dμ = ∫_0^1 (∫_{B̄_{r(t)}} ⟨ν, v⟩ dμ) dt ≥ ∫_0^1 ½ μ(B̄_{r(t)}) dt ≥ ½ μ(B̄_ρ).

5. Annular bound for F (finite-difference form of printed (6)). Steps 3 and 4 give δ·μ(B̄_ρ) ≤ 3 L(F ∩ (B_{ρ+δ} \ B̄_ρ)) for all ρ, δ > 0 with ρ + δ < ρ₂.

6. Annular bound for the complement. For every C¹ compactly supported φ, ∫_E div φ dL = 0 (each ∫ ∂_i φ^i dL vanishes by Fubini and the fundamental theorem of calculus; alternatively by the divergence theorem on a box containing the support). Hence G := E \ F (Borel) satisfies ∫_G div φ = −∫_F div φ = ∫⟨φ, ν⟩ dμ = −∫⟨φ, −ν⟩ dμ for C¹ φ with compact support in D, i.e. (GG) holds for (G, μ, −ν); also |−ν| ≡ 1 and the averages of −ν are −A(r), with ⟨−A(r), −v⟩ = ⟨A(r), v⟩, so (1′) holds for (−ν, −v) with the same ρ₂. Steps 2–5 for (G, −ν, −v) give δ·μ(B̄_ρ) ≤ 3 L((B_{ρ+δ} \ B̄_ρ) \ F) for ρ, δ > 0 with ρ + δ < ρ₂.

7. Upper density (printed (6)). For 0 < ρ < ρ₁ apply step 5 with δ = ρ (then ρ + δ = 2ρ < ρ₂): ρ μ(B̄_ρ) ≤ 3 L(B_{2ρ}) = 3 ω_{m+1} 2^{m+1} ρ^{m+1}, so μ(B̄_ρ) ≤ 3·2^{m+1} ω_{m+1} ρ^m.

8. Conclusion. C := max(3, 3·2^{m+1} ω_{m+1}) ≥ 0 and ρ₁ = ρ₂/2 > 0 satisfy: B̄_{ρ₁} ⊆ B̄_{ρ₀} ⊆ D; for ρ, δ > 0 with ρ + δ < ρ₁ (< ρ₂) both annular inequalities hold by steps 5–6 (3 ≤ C); and μ(B̄_ρ) ≤ C ρ^m for 0 < ρ < ρ₁ by step 7. ∎
proof_key_steps: Normal averages → v give ∫_{B̄_r}⟨ν,v⟩dμ ≥ ½μ(B̄_r) for small r (printed (1)).

Taking δ = ρ gives μ(B̄_ρ) ≤ 3·2^{m+1}ω_{m+1}ρ^m.

subproblems.title: Sobolev inequality for ζ·1_F from the Gauss–Green identity (Simon 4.3 Sobolev step; Ch. 2, 2.5)
subproblems.statement: For every m ≥ 1 there is c > 0 with the following property. Whenever D ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} is open, F ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} is Borel, μ is a Borel measure on ℝ^{m+1} with μ(ℝ^{m+1} \ D) = 0 and μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ D, ν : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m+1} is Borel with |ν(z)| = 1 for every z, and the Gauss–Green identity (GG) ∫_F div φ dL^{m+1} = −∫⟨φ, ν⟩ dμ holds for every C¹ compactly supported φ : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m+1} with tsupport φ ⊆ D (div φ = trace Dφ, L^{m+1} = volume), then (∫_F ζ^{(m+1)/m} dL^{m+1})^{m/(m+1)} ≤ c (∫ ζ dμ + ∫_F |Dζ| dL^{m+1}) for every C¹ compactly supported ζ : ℝ^{m+1} → [0, ∞) with tsupport ζ ⊆ D (|Dζ| the operator norm of the derivative).

Source. The Sobolev step of the printed proof of Simon Ch. 3, 4.3 (chapter-03.txt lines 690–712: (∫(φ1_E)^{(n+1)/n})^{n/(n+1)} ≤ c∫|D(φ1_E)| ≤ c(∫φ dμ_E + ∫_E|Dφ|)), with the mollification Lemma Ch. 2, 2.5 (chapter-02.txt lines 543–596); Mathlib's Gagliardo–Nirenberg–Sobolev inequality (Mathlib/Analysis/FunctionalSpaces/SobolevInequality.lean: `eLpNorm_le_eLpNorm_fderiv_of_eq`, `lintegral_pow_le_pow_lintegral_fderiv`) replaces the citation of [GT01]. Parent proof step 4 (10).

Notation. E := ℝ^{m+1}, n := m + 1 ≥ 2, p := n/(n − 1) = (m+1)/m, L := L^{m+1}.

0. Constant. As finrank E = n ≥ 2, p = n/(n − 1) is the Hölder conjugate of n, and Mathlib's GNS inequality `eLpNorm_le_eLpNorm_fderiv_one` (volume on E) gives a constant c₀ ≥ 0, depending only on E, with ‖w‖_{L^p(L)} ≤ c₀ ‖Dw‖_{L¹(L)} = c₀ ∫|Dw| dL for every C¹ compactly supported w : E → ℝ. Put c := c₀ + 1 > 0; it depends only on m, and the same inequality holds with c in place of c₀. (Rewriting the eLpNorm bound as (∫|w|^p)^{1/p} ≤ c∫|Dw| is routine bookkeeping between eLpNorm, lintegral and the real integral for bounded compactly supported functions.) Now fix D, F, μ, ν as in the statement and ζ ≥ 0 C¹ with compact support, tsupport ζ ⊆ D.

1. BV bound (Simon's |D(φ1_E)| ≤ φ|D1_E| + 1_E|Dφ|). Let u := ζ 1_F (bounded, Borel, compactly supported, u ≥ 0) and M := ∫ζ dμ + ∫_F |Dζ| dL (finite: ζ is continuous with compact support in D and μ(tsupport ζ) < ∞). For every C¹ compactly supported g : E → E with |g| ≤ 1, the field ζg is C¹, compactly supported, tsupport(ζg) ⊆ tsupport ζ ⊆ D, and div(ζg) = ζ div g + Dζ(g). By (GG),
 ∫ u div g dL = ∫_F div(ζg) dL − ∫_F Dζ(g) dL = −∫ ζ ⟨g, ν⟩ dμ − ∫_F Dζ(g) dL,
 hence (*) |∫ u div g dL| ≤ M, because |⟨g, ν⟩| ≤ 1 and |Dζ(g)| ≤ |Dζ|.

2. Mollification. Let η ∈ C_c^∞(E) be even, η ≥ 0, ∫η = 1, spt η ⊆ B_1(0); η_ε(x) := ε^{-n}η(x/ε) and u_ε := η_ε * u, a C^∞ compactly supported function. Claim: ∫|Du_ε| dL ≤ M. Let S be a compact set containing spt u_ε, s := 1_S ∇u_ε/|∇u_ε| on {∇u_ε ≠ 0} and s := 0 elsewhere (bounded, Borel, |s| ≤ 1), and g := η_ε * s (C^∞, compactly supported, |g| ≤ 1). As ∇u_ε = (∇η_ε) * u and ∇η_ε is odd, Fubini gives ∫⟨∇u_ε, s⟩ dL = ∫∫⟨∇η_ε(x − z), s(x)⟩ u(z) dz dx = −∫ u(z) div g(z) dz. Hence ∫|Du_ε| = ∫⟨∇u_ε, s⟩ = −∫ u div g ≤ M by (*).

3. GNS. ‖u_ε‖_{L^p} ≤ c ∫|Du_ε| ≤ c M for every ε > 0.

4. Limit. u ∈ L¹(L), so u_ε → u in L¹ as ε ↓ 0, and u_{ε_k} → u L-a.e. along some ε_k ↓ 0. By Fatou, ∫|u|^p dL ≤ liminf_k ∫|u_{ε_k}|^p dL ≤ (cM)^p. Since u = ζ1_F ≥ 0, ∫|u|^p dL = ∫_F ζ^{(m+1)/m} dL; taking the power 1/p = m/(m+1) gives (∫_F ζ^{(m+1)/m} dL)^{m/(m+1)} ≤ c(∫ζ dμ + ∫_F |Dζ| dL). ∎
proof_key_steps: Mathlib GNS constant c_n for C¹ compactly supported functions on ℝ^{m+1}, n = m+1 ≥ 2.
Gauss–Green applied to ζg gives |∫ζ1_F div g| ≤ ∫ζdμ + ∫_F|Dζ| for |g| ≤ 1.
For a symmetric mollifier, ∫|D(η_ε * ζ1_F)| ≤ the same bound, by duality with g = η_ε * s.
GNS applied to the mollifications.
Fatou along an a.e.-convergent sequence ε_k ↓ 0.

subproblems.title: Two-sided volume density bounds at a reduced-boundary point (De Giorgi; Simon 4.3 (10)–(11))
subproblems.statement: Let m ≥ 1. Suppose D ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} is open, F ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} is Borel, μ is a Borel measure on ℝ^{m+1} with μ(ℝ^{m+1} \ D) = 0 and μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ D, ν : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m+1} is Borel with |ν(z)| = 1 for every z, and the Gauss–Green identity (GG) ∫_F div φ dL^{m+1} = −∫⟨φ, ν⟩ dμ holds for every C¹ compactly supported φ : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m+1} with tsupport φ ⊆ D (div φ = trace Dφ, L^{m+1} = volume). Let y ∈ D and v ∈ ℝ^{m+1} with |v| = 1 be such that the normal averages A(ρ) := μ(B̄_ρ(y))_ℝ^{-1} ∫_{B̄_ρ(y)} ν dμ converge to v as ρ ↓ 0 (μ(·)_ℝ = ENNReal.toReal, 0^{-1} = 0). Then there are c > 0 and ρ₂ > 0 such that L^{m+1}(F ∩ B_ρ(y)) ≥ c ρ^{m+1} and L^{m+1}(B_ρ(y) \ F) ≥ c ρ^{m+1} for all 0 < ρ < ρ₂.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Printed proof of Simon Ch. 3, 4.3, (10)–(11) (chapter-03.txt lines 690–733); parent proof step 4 (10)–(11). Departure (rigour only): the a.e. differential inequality and the printed "Integration … then implies (10)" are replaced by a finite-difference inequality and an explicit discrete integration (AM–GM), so no differentiability of ρ ↦ L(F ∩ B_ρ) is used. Dependencies: cutoff_estimates (Submission.codim1_rdo_dg_cutoff_estimates) and sobolev_perimeter (Submission.codim1_rdo_dg_sobolev_perimeter).

Notation. E := ℝ^{m+1}, L := L^{m+1}, B_r := B_r(y), B̄_r := B̄_r(y), A(r) := μ(B̄_r)_ℝ^{-1}∫_{B̄_r} ν dμ, V(r) := L(F ∩ B̄_r), V^c(r) := L(B̄_r \ F).

1. Inputs. cutoff_estimates gives ρ₁ > 0 and C₁ ≥ 0 with B̄_{ρ₁} ⊆ D and, for all ρ, δ > 0 with ρ + δ < ρ₁,
 (a) δ μ(B̄_ρ) ≤ C₁ L(F ∩ (B_{ρ+δ} \ B̄_ρ)),  (b) δ μ(B̄_ρ) ≤ C₁ L((B_{ρ+δ} \ B̄_ρ) \ F).
 sobolev_perimeter (m ≥ 1) gives c_S > 0.

2. Positivity. Since ⟨A(r), v⟩ → 1, A(r) ≠ 0 for small r, so μ(B̄_r) > 0 for small r and, by monotonicity, for every r > 0. For 0 < r < ρ₁, (a) with ρ = δ = r/2 gives (r/2) μ(B̄_{r/2}) ≤ C₁ V(r); hence C₁ > 0 and V(r) > 0. Likewise (b) gives V^c(r) > 0. V and V^c are finite and nondecreasing.

3. Finite-difference inequality (printed (10), first displays). Let ρ, δ > 0 with ρ + 2δ < ρ₁. Let h(t) := 1 for t ≤ 0, h(t) := 1 − 3t² + 2t³ for 0 ≤ t ≤ 1, h(t) := 0 for t ≥ 1; h is C¹, nonincreasing, h′(t) = −6t(1 − t) on [0, 1] and h′ = 0 elsewhere, so h′(0) = h′(1) = 0 and |h′| ≤ 3/2. Put ζ(z) := h((|z − y| − ρ)/δ). ζ ≡ 1 on the open ball B_ρ (a neighbourhood of y), and on E \ {y} it is a composition of C¹ maps, so ζ is C¹ on E; 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1, ζ = 1 on B̄_ρ, tsupport ζ ⊆ B̄_{ρ+δ} ⊆ B̄_{ρ₁} ⊆ D, and ∇ζ(z) = δ^{-1} h′((|z − y| − ρ)/δ)(z − y)/|z − y| vanishes outside B_{ρ+δ} \ B̄_ρ, with |∇ζ| ≤ 3/(2δ). By sobolev_perimeter,
 V(ρ)^{m/(m+1)} ≤ (∫_F ζ^{(m+1)/m} dL)^{m/(m+1)} ≤ c_S (∫ζ dμ + ∫_F |∇ζ| dL).
 Here ∫ζ dμ ≤ μ(B̄_{ρ+δ}) ≤ (C₁/δ) L(F ∩ (B_{ρ+2δ} \ B̄_{ρ+δ})) by (a) at radius ρ + δ, and ∫_F |∇ζ| ≤ (3/(2δ)) L(F ∩ (B_{ρ+δ} \ B̄_ρ)). The two annuli are disjoint subsets of B̄_{ρ+2δ} \ B̄_ρ, so V(ρ)^{m/(m+1)} ≤ (c_S(C₁ + 3/2)/δ)(V(ρ + 2δ) − V(ρ)). With δ′ := 2δ and K := 2c_S(C₁ + 3/2) > 0:
 (♦) V(ρ)^{m/(m+1)} ≤ (K/δ′)(V(ρ + δ′) − V(ρ)) whenever ρ, δ′ > 0 and ρ + δ′ < ρ₁.

4. Discrete integration (printed "Integration … implies (10)"). Claim: V(ρ) ≥ (ρ/(2K(m+1)))^{m+1} for 0 < ρ < ρ₁. Let W := V^{1/(m+1)}, positive and nondecreasing on (0, ρ₁). Fix ρ and N ≥ 1, δ := ρ/(2N), ρ_j := ρ/2 + jδ (0 ≤ j ≤ N), so ρ_N = ρ < ρ₁. For j < N put a := W(ρ_{j+1}) ≥ b := W(ρ_j) > 0. By (♦) and a^{m+1} − b^{m+1} ≤ (m+1)a^m(a − b): b^m ≤ (K/δ)(m+1)a^m(a − b), i.e. W(ρ_{j+1}) − W(ρ_j) ≥ (δ/(K(m+1)))(W(ρ_j)/W(ρ_{j+1}))^m. Summing over j and using AM–GM (Σ_j x_j ≥ N(Π_j x_j)^{1/N}, with Π_j W(ρ_j)/W(ρ_{j+1}) = W(ρ/2)/W(ρ)):
 W(ρ) − W(ρ/2) ≥ (ρ/(2K(m+1))) (W(ρ/2)/W(ρ))^{m/N}.
 Letting N → ∞ (W(ρ/2) > 0): W(ρ) ≥ W(ρ) − W(ρ/2) ≥ ρ/(2K(m+1)).

5. Complement (printed (11): "Repeating the same argument with U \ E in place of E"). For C¹ compactly supported φ, ∫_E div φ dL = 0: in standard coordinates div φ = Σ_i ∂_i φ^i, and for each i, Fubini writes ∫ ∂_i φ^i dL as an iterated integral whose innermost integral ∫_ℝ ∂_i φ^i dx_i vanishes by the fundamental theorem of calculus, φ^i having compact support. Hence G := E \ F satisfies (GG) with (μ, −ν): ∫_G div φ = ∫⟨φ, ν⟩ dμ = −∫⟨φ, −ν⟩ dμ. Hence sobolev_perimeter applies to (D, G, μ, −ν) with the same c_S, and (b) is (a) for G. Steps 3–4 for V^c (with the same K) give V^c(ρ) ≥ (ρ/(2K(m+1)))^{m+1} for 0 < ρ < ρ₁.

6. Conclusion. For 0 < ρ < ρ₁: L(F ∩ B_ρ) ≥ V(ρ/2) ≥ (ρ/(4K(m+1)))^{m+1} and L(B_ρ \ F) ≥ V^c(ρ/2) ≥ (ρ/(4K(m+1)))^{m+1}. Take c := (4K(m+1))^{-(m+1)} > 0 and ρ₂ := ρ₁. ∎
proof_key_steps: cutoff_estimates: annular bounds δμ(B̄_ρ) ≤ C₁L(F ∩ annulus) and the same for the complement.
Positivity of V(r) = L(F ∩ B̄_r(y)) and of L(B̄_r(y) ∖ F).
sobolev_perimeter with a C¹ cut-off gives V(ρ)^{m/(m+1)} ≤ (K/δ)(V(ρ+δ) − V(ρ)).
Discrete integration with AM–GM gives V(ρ) ≥ (ρ/(2K(m+1)))^{m+1}.
The same argument for ℝ^{m+1} ∖ F with normal −ν.

subproblems.title: Compactness for sets of locally uniformly bounded perimeter (Simon Ch. 2, 2.6)
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ and let F_k ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} (k ∈ ℕ) be Borel sets such that for every R > 0 there is C_R ∈ ℝ with ∫_{F_k} div g dL^{m+1} ≤ C_R for all sufficiently large k and every C¹ compactly supported g : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m+1} with tsupport g ⊆ B_R(0) and |g| ≤ 1. Then there are a strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ and a Borel set F₀ ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} with L^{m+1}((F_{ψ(j)} Δ F₀) ∩ B_R(0)) → 0 as j → ∞ for every R ∈ ℝ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (Fs : ℕ → Set (Euclid (m + 1))), (∀ k, MeasurableSet (Fs k)) → (∀ R : ℝ, 0 < R → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ k in atTop, ∀ g : Euclid (m + 1) → Euclid (m + 1), ContDiff ℝ 1 g → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ ball (0 : Euclid (m + 1)) R → (∀ z, ‖g z‖ ≤ 1) → ∫ z in Fs k, LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m + 1)) (fderiv ℝ g z : Euclid (m + 1) →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid (m + 1)) ≤ C) → ∃ (ψ : ℕ → ℕ) (F₀ : Set (Euclid (m + 1))), StrictMono ψ ∧ MeasurableSet F₀ ∧ ∀ R : ℝ, Tendsto (fun j => volume (symmDiff (Fs (ψ j)) F₀ ∩ ball (0 : Euclid (m + 1)) R)) atTop (𝓝 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Simon Ch. 2, 2.6 (Compactness Theorem for BV functions, chapter-02.txt lines 598–626) for u_k = 1_{F_k} on U = ℝ^{m+1}; the precompactness step, which the book delegates to [GT01, Theorem 7.22], is written out (mollification and Arzelà–Ascoli). Parent proof step 4 (7).

Notation. E := ℝ^{m+1}, L := L^{m+1}, B_R := B_R(0), u_k := 1_{F_k}, ‖f‖_{1,R} := ∫_{B_R} |f| dL. Fix an even mollifier η ∈ C_c^∞(E) (η ≥ 0, ∫η = 1, spt η ⊆ B_1) and η_ε(x) := ε^{-(m+1)}η(x/ε). For R > 0 let k_R be such that the hypothesis holds with the constant C_R for all k ≥ k_R; g = 0 shows C_R ≥ 0.

1. Mollification estimate. For R > 0, 0 < ε < 1 and k ≥ k_{R+1}: ‖u_k − η_ε * u_k‖_{1,R} ≤ ε C_{R+1}.
 Proof. Let ψ ∈ C_c^∞(E) with tsupport ψ ⊆ B_R and |ψ| ≤ 1. By evenness of η, ∫(u_k − η_ε * u_k)ψ = ∫ u_k(ψ − η_ε * ψ). Now ψ(x) − (η_ε * ψ)(x) = ∫ η_ε(w)(ψ(x) − ψ(x − w)) dw = div X(x) with X(x) := ∫ η_ε(w) ∫_0^1 ψ(x − tw) w dt dw (differentiation under the integral gives div X(x) = ∫ η_ε(w) ∫_0^1 ⟨∇ψ(x − tw), w⟩ dt dw). X is C^∞, |X| ≤ ε (|w| ≤ ε on spt η_ε), and tsupport X ⊆ B̄_{R+ε} ⊆ B_{R+1}. Applying the hypothesis to ±X/ε: |∫ u_k(ψ − η_ε * ψ)| = |∫_{F_k} div X| ≤ ε C_{R+1}. Finally ‖f‖_{1,R} = sup{∫ fψ : ψ as above} for f ∈ L¹_loc: the admissible functions ψ_j := η_{δ_j} * (1_{B_{R−2δ_j}} sgn f), δ_j ↓ 0, converge a.e. on B_R to sgn f along a subsequence, and dominated convergence applies.

2. Equicontinuity. For fixed ε the functions u_{k,ε} := η_ε * u_k satisfy 0 ≤ u_{k,ε} ≤ 1 and |∇u_{k,ε}| = |(∇η_ε) * u_k| ≤ ‖∇η_ε‖_{L¹} =: Λ_ε. By Arzelà–Ascoli (or directly: a bounded Λ_ε-Lipschitz function on B̄_R is determined up to sup-error θ by its values on a finite θ/Λ_ε-net, rounded to multiples of θ), {u_{k,ε}|_{B̄_R} : k ∈ ℕ} is totally bounded in the sup norm, hence in L¹(B_R) since ‖f‖_{1,R} ≤ L(B_R) sup_{B_R}|f|.

3. Total boundedness. Fix R > 0 and θ > 0 and choose ε ∈ (0, 1) with ε C_{R+1} < θ/3. By step 1, ‖u_k − u_{k,ε}‖_{1,R} < θ/3 for k ≥ k_{R+1}; by step 2 the u_{k,ε} lie in finitely many L¹(B_R)-balls of radius θ/3. So {u_k|_{B_R} : k ≥ k_{R+1}} lies in finitely many balls of radius 2θ/3; adding the finitely many k < k_{R+1}, {u_k|_{B_R} : k ∈ ℕ} is totally bounded in L¹(B_R).

4. Diagonal extraction. L¹(B_R) is complete, so every sequence in a totally bounded subset has a Cauchy, hence convergent, subsequence. Apply this successively for R = 1, 2, 3, … to nested subsequences and take the diagonal sequence ψ (strictly increasing): for every integer N ≥ 1, u_{ψ(j)}|_{B_N} converges in L¹(B_N) to some w_N, and w_{N+1} = w_N a.e. on B_N.

5. The limit is an indicator. For each N a further subsequence converges a.e. on B_N; since u_k ∈ {0, 1}, w_N ∈ {0, 1} a.e. on B_N. Choose Borel representatives and set F₀ := ⋃_N ((B_N \ B_{N−1}) ∩ {w_N = 1}) (B_0 := ∅), a Borel set with 1_{F₀} = w_N a.e. on B_N for every N. For R > 0 choose an integer N ≥ R: L((F_{ψ(j)} Δ F₀) ∩ B_R) = ‖u_{ψ(j)} − 1_{F₀}‖_{1,R} ≤ ‖u_{ψ(j)} − w_N‖_{1,N} → 0. For R ≤ 0, B_R = ∅ and the quantity is 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Duality and ψ − η_ε*ψ = div X with |X| ≤ ε give ‖1_{F_k} − η_ε*1_{F_k}‖_{L¹(B_R)} ≤ εC_{R+1}.
Mollified indicators are uniformly bounded and uniformly Lipschitz, hence totally bounded (Arzelà–Ascoli).
So {1_{F_k}} is totally bounded in L¹(B_R) for each R.
Completeness and a diagonal argument give an L¹_loc-convergent subsequence.
L¹ limits of indicators are indicators of a Borel set F₀.

subproblems.title: A set with vanishing tangential and nonpositive normal distributional derivative is a half-space (Simon 4.3 (8)–(9))
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, v ∈ ℝ^{m+1} with |v| = 1, and F₀ ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} Borel. Suppose ∫_{F₀} Dζ(z)(w) dL^{m+1}(z) = 0 for every C¹ compactly supported ζ : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ and every w with ⟨w, v⟩ = 0, and ∫_{F₀} Dζ(z)(v) dL^{m+1}(z) ≤ 0 for every such ζ with ζ ≥ 0. Then L^{m+1}(F₀) = 0, or L^{m+1}(ℝ^{m+1} \ F₀) = 0, or there is c ∈ ℝ with L^{m+1}(F₀ Δ {z : ⟨z, v⟩ > c}) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (F₀ : Set (Euclid (m + 1))) (v : Euclid (m + 1)), ‖v‖ = 1 → MeasurableSet F₀ → (∀ ζ : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 ζ → HasCompactSupport ζ → ∀ w : Euclid (m + 1), inner ℝ w v = 0 → ∫ z in F₀, fderiv ℝ ζ z w = 0) → (∀ ζ : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 ζ → HasCompactSupport ζ → (∀ z, 0 ≤ ζ z) → ∫ z in F₀, fderiv ℝ ζ z v ≤ 0) → volume F₀ = 0 ∨ volume F₀ᶜ = 0 ∨ ∃ c : ℝ, volume (symmDiff F₀ {z | c < inner ℝ z v}) = 0

Source. Printed proof of Simon Ch. 3, 4.3, (8)–(9) (chapter-03.txt lines 664–690): "it follows that F = ℝ^n × H … H is non-decreasing on ℝ, hence (9)". Erratum (parent proof): for the inward normal the limit set is {x^{n+1} > λ}, not {x^{n+1} < λ}. The printed "it follows that" is made rigorous by translation invariance and Lebesgue density points. Parent proof step 4 (8)–(9).

Notation. E := ℝ^{m+1}, L := L^{m+1}, u := 1_{F₀}, ∂_w ζ := Dζ(·)(w).

1. Translation identity. For ζ ∈ C¹_c(E; ℝ), w ∈ E, t ∈ ℝ: ζ(z − tw) − ζ(z) = −∫_0^t (∂_w ζ)(z − sw) ds, and ∂_w[ζ(· − sw)] = (∂_w ζ)(· − sw). The integrand is bounded and vanishes outside a compact subset of [min(0,t), max(0,t)] × E, so by Fubini
 ∫ u(z)(ζ(z − tw) − ζ(z)) dz = −∫_0^t (∫_{F₀} ∂_w[ζ(· − sw)](z) dz) ds.

2. Tangential invariance. If ⟨w, v⟩ = 0, every inner integral vanishes by the first hypothesis applied to the C¹_c function ζ(· − sw). Substituting z ↦ z + tw (L is translation invariant) gives ∫ (u(z + tw) − u(z)) ζ(z) dz = 0 for all ζ ∈ C¹_c, in particular for all ζ ∈ C_c^∞. By the fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations (Mathlib `ae_eq_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq`; u and u(· + tw) are locally integrable), u(· + tw) = u L-a.e.

3. Normal monotonicity. Let t ≥ 0 and ζ ∈ C¹_c with ζ ≥ 0. Each ζ(· − sv) ≥ 0, so by the second hypothesis each inner integral in step 1 (with w = v) is ≤ 0, and ∫ (u(z + tv) − u(z)) ζ(z) dz ≥ 0. This forces f := u(· + tv) − u ≥ 0 a.e.: for R > 0 let S := {f < 0} ∩ B_R(0) and ζ_j := η_{1/j} * 1_S (η an even mollifier); ζ_j ∈ C_c^∞, 0 ≤ ζ_j ≤ 1, ζ_j → 1_S in L¹ and a.e. along a subsequence, and by dominated convergence (|fζ_j| ≤ |f| 1_{B_{R+1}(0)}) ∫_S f = lim ∫ f ζ_j ≥ 0; since f < 0 on S, L(S) = 0.

4. Monotonicity in all directions a with ⟨a, v⟩ ≥ 0. Write a = tv + w with t := ⟨a, v⟩ ≥ 0 and w := a − tv, so ⟨w, v⟩ = 0 (|v| = 1). For a.e. z, u(z + a) = u((z + w) + tv) ≥ u(z + w) = u(z): the inequality holds for a.e. z because {z′ : u(z′ + tv) < u(z′)} is null and translation by w preserves null sets, and the equality is step 2. So u(· + a) ≥ u a.e.

5. Density points. By the Lebesgue density theorem (Mathlib `Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div`), for a.e. z ∈ F₀ the ratio L(F₀ ∩ B̄_r(z))/L(B̄_r(z)) → 1 and for a.e. z ∉ F₀ it → 0, as r ↓ 0. Let A₁ (resp. A₀) be the set where it tends to 1 (resp. 0). Claim: ⟨z₀, v⟩ < ⟨z₁, v⟩ for all z₁ ∈ A₁, z₀ ∈ A₀. Otherwise a := z₀ − z₁ has ⟨a, v⟩ ≥ 0, and by step 4, for every r > 0, L(F₀ ∩ B̄_r(z₀)) = ∫_{B̄_r(z₁)} u(z + a) dz ≥ ∫_{B̄_r(z₁)} u(z) dz = L(F₀ ∩ B̄_r(z₁)); dividing by L(B̄_r(z₀)) = L(B̄_r(z₁)) and letting r ↓ 0 gives 0 ≥ 1.

6. Conclusion. If A₁ = ∅ then L(F₀) = 0 (a.e. point of F₀ lies in A₁). If A₀ = ∅ then L(E \ F₀) = 0. Otherwise c := sup{⟨z₀, v⟩ : z₀ ∈ A₀} is finite (bounded above by ⟨z₁, v⟩ for any z₁ ∈ A₁), and ⟨z₁, v⟩ ≥ c for every z₁ ∈ A₁. Then F₀ \ {⟨z, v⟩ > c} ⊆ (F₀ \ A₁) ∪ {⟨z, v⟩ = c} and {⟨z, v⟩ > c} \ F₀ ⊆ (E \ F₀) \ A₀. All three sets are L-null (the hyperplane {⟨z, v⟩ = c} is null as v ≠ 0), so L(F₀ Δ {z : ⟨z, v⟩ > c}) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Translation identity ∫u(ζ(·−tw) − ζ) = −∫_0^t∫_{F₀}∂_w[ζ(·−sw)] ds.
Tangential directions: u(·+tw) = u a.e. by the fundamental lemma.
Normal direction: u(·+tv) ≥ u a.e. for t ≥ 0.
Hence u(·+a) ≥ u a.e. whenever ⟨a,v⟩ ≥ 0.
Density points of F₀ lie strictly above density points of the complement in the v-direction.
Lebesgue density theorem: F₀ is null, co-null, or {⟨z,v⟩ > c} up to null sets.

subproblems.title: Blow-ups at a reduced-boundary point converge to the half-space (De Giorgi; Simon 4.3 (‡))
subproblems.statement: Let m ≥ 1. Suppose D ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} is open, F ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} is Borel, μ is a Borel measure on ℝ^{m+1} with μ(ℝ^{m+1} \ D) = 0 and μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ D, ν : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m+1} is Borel with |ν(z)| = 1 for every z, and the Gauss–Green identity (GG) ∫_F div φ dL^{m+1} = −∫⟨φ, ν⟩ dμ holds for every C¹ compactly supported φ : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m+1} with tsupport φ ⊆ D (div φ = trace Dφ, L^{m+1} = volume). Let y ∈ D and v ∈ ℝ^{m+1} with |v| = 1 be such that the normal averages A(ρ) := μ(B̄_ρ(y))_ℝ^{-1} ∫_{B̄_ρ(y)} ν dμ converge to v as ρ ↓ 0 (μ(·)_ℝ = ENNReal.toReal, 0^{-1} = 0). For r > 0 put F_{y,r} := {w : y + r w ∈ F}. Then for every R ∈ ℝ, L^{m+1}((F_{y,r} Δ {w : ⟨w, v⟩ > 0}) ∩ B_R(0)) → 0 as r ↓ 0.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Printed proof of Simon Ch. 3, 4.3, (7)–(11) and the paragraph "Now given any sequence λ_k ↓ 0 …" (chapter-03.txt lines 652–744); parent proof step 4 (7)–(11). Erratum: for the inward normal ν the limit is {x : ⟨x, ν_E(0)⟩ > 0}; the OCR's "{x^{n+1} < λ}" has the inequality reversed. Dependencies: cutoff_estimates, volume_density_lower, bv_compactness, halfspace_rigidity.

Notation. E := ℝ^{m+1}, L := L^{m+1}, B_s := B_s(0); for r > 0, F_r := F_{y,r} = {w : y + rw ∈ F} (Borel); H := {w : ⟨w, v⟩ > 0}; A(ρ) := μ(B̄_ρ(y))_ℝ^{-1} ∫_{B̄_ρ(y)} ν dμ and ε(ρ) := 1 − ⟨A(ρ), v⟩ → 0 as ρ ↓ 0.

1. Data. cutoff_estimates gives ρ₁ > 0, C₁ ≥ 0 with B̄_{ρ₁}(y) ⊆ D and μ(B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ C₁ρ^m for 0 < ρ < ρ₁. volume_density_lower gives c₂, ρ₂ > 0 with L(F ∩ B_ρ(y)) ≥ c₂ρ^{m+1} and L(B_ρ(y) \ F) ≥ c₂ρ^{m+1} for 0 < ρ < ρ₂.

2. Rescaled Gauss–Green (printed (8)). Let g : E → E be C¹ with tsupport g ⊆ B_R, R > 0, and 0 < r < ρ₁/R. Then φ(z) := g((z − y)/r) is C¹, tsupport φ ⊆ y + r·tsupport g ⊆ B_{rR}(y) ⊆ D, and div φ(z) = r^{-1}(div g)((z − y)/r). By (GG) and the substitution z = y + rw (Jacobian r^{m+1}):
 (2a) ∫_{F_r} div g dL = r^{-m} ∫_F div φ dL = −r^{-m} ∫ ⟨g((z − y)/r), ν(z)⟩ dμ(z);
 in particular |∫_{F_r} div g| ≤ ‖g‖_∞ r^{-m} μ(B̄_{rR}(y)) ≤ ‖g‖_∞ C₁ R^m.

3. Normal concentration (printed (1)–(2)). For 0 < ρ < ρ₁: ∫_{B̄_ρ(y)} (1 − ⟨ν, v⟩) dμ = μ(B̄_ρ(y)) ε(ρ) (both sides vanish if μ(B̄_ρ(y)) = 0), and 1 − ⟨ν, v⟩ ≥ 0. If ⟨w, v⟩ = 0 and |w| = 1 then ⟨ν, w⟩² ≤ 1 − ⟨ν, v⟩² ≤ 2(1 − ⟨ν, v⟩), so by Cauchy–Schwarz ∫_{B̄_ρ(y)} |⟨ν, w⟩| dμ ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y)) (2ε(ρ))^{1/2}.

4. Compactness (printed (7)). Let r_k ↓ 0. For R > 0 and every k with r_k R < ρ₁, step 2 gives ∫_{F_{r_k}} div g ≤ C₁R^m for every C¹ compactly supported g with tsupport g ⊆ B_R and |g| ≤ 1. By bv_compactness there are a subsequence r_{k_j} and a Borel set F₀ with L((F_{r_{k_j}} Δ F₀) ∩ B_R) → 0 for every R; hence ∫_{F_{r_{k_j}}} f → ∫_{F₀} f for every bounded Borel f vanishing outside some B_R.

5. The limit is a half-space (printed (8)–(9)). Let ζ ∈ C¹_c(E; ℝ) with tsupport ζ ⊆ B_R.
 (a) For w ≠ 0 with ⟨w, v⟩ = 0, g := ζ w has div g = Dζ(w). By (2a) and step 3, |∫_{F_r} Dζ(w)| ≤ ‖ζ‖_∞ |w| r^{-m} ∫_{B̄_{rR}(y)} |⟨ν, w/|w|⟩| dμ ≤ ‖ζ‖_∞ |w| C₁ R^m (2ε(rR))^{1/2} → 0 as r ↓ 0. Hence ∫_{F₀} Dζ(w) = 0 (trivially also for w = 0).
 (b) If ζ ≥ 0, g := ζ v has div g = Dζ(v), and by (2a), ∫_{F_r} Dζ(v) = −r^{-m} ∫ ζ((z − y)/r) dμ(z) + r^{-m} ∫ ζ((z − y)/r)(1 − ⟨ν(z), v⟩) dμ(z) ≤ ‖ζ‖_∞ C₁ R^m ε(rR) → 0. Hence ∫_{F₀} Dζ(v) ≤ 0.
 By halfspace_rigidity: L(F₀) = 0, or L(E \ F₀) = 0, or L(F₀ Δ {⟨w, v⟩ > c}) = 0 for some c ∈ ℝ.

6. c = 0 (printed (10)–(11)). For s > 0 and 0 < r < ρ₂/s, the substitution gives L(F_r ∩ B_s) = r^{-(m+1)} L(F ∩ B_{rs}(y)) ≥ c₂ s^{m+1} and L(B_s \ F_r) = r^{-(m+1)} L(B_{rs}(y) \ F) ≥ c₂ s^{m+1}. Passing to the limit along r_{k_j}: L(F₀ ∩ B_s) ≥ c₂ s^{m+1} > 0 and L(B_s \ F₀) ≥ c₂ s^{m+1} > 0 for every s > 0. This excludes L(F₀) = 0 and L(E \ F₀) = 0. If c > 0, then B_s ∩ {⟨w, v⟩ > c} = ∅ for s < c, contradicting L(F₀ ∩ B_s) > 0; if c < 0, then B_s ⊆ {⟨w, v⟩ > c} for s < −c, contradicting L(B_s \ F₀) > 0. Hence c = 0 and L(F₀ Δ H) = 0.

7. Whole family ("Now given any sequence…"). Fix R; if R ≤ 0 the quantity is 0. Otherwise suppose a(r) := L((F_r Δ H) ∩ B_R) does not tend to 0 as r ↓ 0: there are θ > 0 and r_k ↓ 0 with a(r_k) ≥ θ. Steps 4–6 give a subsequence with F_{r_{k_j}} → F₀ in L¹_loc and L(F₀ Δ H) = 0, so a(r_{k_j}) ≤ L((F_{r_{k_j}} Δ F₀) ∩ B_R) + L(F₀ Δ H) → 0, a contradiction. ∎
proof_key_steps: Rescaled Gauss–Green: ∫_{F_r} div g = −r^{-m}∫⟨g((z−y)/r),ν⟩dμ; upper density gives the perimeter bound C₁R^m.
Normal averages → v make ∫_{B̄_ρ}(1−⟨ν,v⟩)dμ and the tangential components o(μ(B̄_ρ)).
bv_compactness extracts L¹_loc limits F₀ of blow-ups along any r_k ↓ 0.
Limits have zero tangential and nonpositive normal derivative, so halfspace_rigidity makes them {⟨w,v⟩ > c} or trivial.
Scale-invariant two-sided volume bounds from volume_density_lower force c = 0.
Uniqueness of the limit gives convergence of the whole family r ↓ 0.

subproblems.title: Tangent measure of the Gauss–Green measure is H^m on ν(y)^⊥ almost everywhere (De Giorgi; Simon 4.3 (†))
subproblems.statement: Let m ≥ 1. Suppose D ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} is open, F ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} is Borel, μ is a Borel measure on ℝ^{m+1} with μ(ℝ^{m+1} \ D) = 0 and μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ D, ν : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m+1} is Borel with |ν(z)| = 1 for every z, and the Gauss–Green identity (GG) ∫_F div φ dL^{m+1} = −∫⟨φ, ν⟩ dμ holds for every C¹ compactly supported φ : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m+1} with tsupport φ ⊆ D (div φ = trace Dφ, L^{m+1} = volume). Then for μ-a.e. y and every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ, r^{-m} ∫ f(r^{-1}(z − y)) dμ(z) → ∫_{(span{ν(y)})^⊥} f dH^m as r ↓ 0, where H^m = μHE[m].

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Last paragraph of the printed proof of Simon Ch. 3, 4.3 ("Then by 4.1, (1) and (2) we have … → H^n⌞{x^{n+1} = 0}", chapter-03.txt lines 734–746), i.e. 4.3(†); parent proof step 4 (12). The parent's lower-semicontinuity bullet is not needed: the splitting f = f⟨ν, v⟩ + f(1 − ⟨ν, v⟩) used below is exactly the printed appeal to 4.1 and (1). Dependencies: normal_average_ae, cutoff_estimates, blowup_halfspace.

Notation. E := ℝ^{m+1}, L := L^{m+1}, H^m := μHE[m], P_v := (span{v})^⊥, H_v := {w : ⟨w, v⟩ > 0}, F_r := {w : y + rw ∈ F}, A(ρ) := μ(B̄_ρ(y))_ℝ^{-1} ∫_{B̄_ρ(y)} ν dμ, ε(ρ) := 1 − ⟨A(ρ), v⟩, ω_m := unitBallVolume m = L^m(B_1(0)).

1. Good points. By normal_average_ae, for μ-a.e. y: y ∈ D and A(ρ) → ν(y) as ρ ↓ 0. Fix such y and put v := ν(y), so |v| = 1 and ε(ρ) → 0. By cutoff_estimates: ρ₁ > 0 and C₁ with B̄_{ρ₁}(y) ⊆ D and μ(B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ C₁ρ^m for 0 < ρ < ρ₁. By blowup_halfspace: L((F_r Δ H_v) ∩ B_R(0)) → 0 as r ↓ 0, for every R.

2. Gauss–Green for the half-space. For every C¹ compactly supported g : E → E, ∫_{H_v} div g dL = −∫_{P_v} ⟨g, v⟩ dH^m. Proof: complete v to an orthonormal basis (b_1, …, b_m, b_{m+1} = v) of E. The coordinate map Ψ(z) := (⟨z, b_i⟩)_{i ≤ m+1} is a linear isometry E → ℝ^{m+1} preserving Lebesgue measure (Mathlib `OrthonormalBasis.measurePreserving_repr`); it maps H_v onto {x : x_{m+1} > 0} and P_v onto {x_{m+1} = 0}, and the map ι : ℝ^m → P_v, ι(x′) := Σ_{i ≤ m} x′_i b_i, is a linear isometry onto P_v carrying L^m to H^m⌞P_v (μHE[m] is isometry invariant and equals volume on ℝ^m). In this basis div g = Σ_{i ≤ m+1} D⟨g, b_i⟩(b_i) (trace in an orthonormal basis), and G_i(x) := ⟨g(Ψ^{-1}x), b_i⟩ is C¹ with compact support on ℝ^{m+1}, with D⟨g, b_i⟩(b_i) ∘ Ψ^{-1} = ∂_{x_i} G_i. Use Fubini for the product decomposition ℝ^{m+1} = ℝ^m × ℝ of Lebesgue measure (only measure preservation is used, not the product norm). For i ≤ m, ∫_{H_v} D⟨g, b_i⟩(b_i) dL = ∫_{x_{m+1} > 0} ∂_{x_i} G_i dx = 0, because for fixed values of the other coordinates the integral of ∂_{x_i} G_i over the line in the x_i-direction vanishes (fundamental theorem of calculus, compact support). For i = m + 1, ∫_{H_v} D⟨g, v⟩(v) dL = ∫_{ℝ^m} ∫_0^∞ ∂_t G_{m+1}(x′, t) dt dx′ = −∫_{ℝ^m} G_{m+1}(x′, 0) dx′ = −∫_{P_v} ⟨g, v⟩ dH^m.

3. Vector convergence. Let g be C¹ with tsupport g ⊆ B_R(0) and 0 < r < ρ₁/R. Then φ(z) := g((z − y)/r) is C¹ with compact support, tsupport φ ⊆ y + r·tsupport g ⊆ B_{rR}(y) ⊆ B̄_{ρ₁}(y) ⊆ D, and div φ(z) = r^{-1}(div g)((z − y)/r). By (GG) and the substitution z = y + rw (Jacobian r^{m+1}; F_r = {w : y + rw ∈ F}): r^m ∫_{F_r} div g dL = ∫_F div φ dL = −∫ ⟨g((z − y)/r), ν(z)⟩ dμ(z), i.e. r^{-m} ∫ ⟨g((z − y)/r), ν(z)⟩ dμ(z) = −∫_{F_r} div g dL. Since |∫_{F_r} div g − ∫_{H_v} div g| ≤ ‖div g‖_∞ L((F_r Δ H_v) ∩ B_R(0)) → 0, step 2 gives
 (3a) r^{-m} ∫ ⟨g((z − y)/r), ν(z)⟩ dμ(z) → ∫_{P_v} ⟨g, v⟩ dH^m as r ↓ 0.

4. C¹ scalar test functions. Let f ∈ C¹_c(E; ℝ) with tsupport f ⊆ B_R(0). For 0 < r < ρ₁/R,
 r^{-m} ∫ f((z − y)/r) dμ = r^{-m} ∫ f((z − y)/r)⟨ν(z), v⟩ dμ + r^{-m} ∫ f((z − y)/r)(1 − ⟨ν(z), v⟩) dμ.
 By (3a) with g := f v (⟨fv, v⟩ = f) the first term tends to ∫_{P_v} f dH^m. Since 1 − ⟨ν, v⟩ ≥ 0 and ∫_{B̄_ρ(y)} (1 − ⟨ν, v⟩) dμ = μ(B̄_ρ(y)) ε(ρ), the second term is at most ‖f‖_∞ r^{-m} μ(B̄_{rR}(y)) ε(rR) ≤ ‖f‖_∞ C₁ R^m ε(rR) → 0 in absolute value.

5. Continuous test functions. Let f be continuous with tsupport f ⊆ B_R(0) and θ > 0. Mollifying, there is f_θ ∈ C_c^∞ with tsupport f_θ ⊆ B_{R+1}(0) and ‖f − f_θ‖_∞ ≤ θ. For 0 < r < ρ₁/(R+1): |r^{-m} ∫ (f − f_θ)((z − y)/r) dμ| ≤ θ r^{-m} μ(B̄_{r(R+1)}(y)) ≤ θ C₁ (R+1)^m, and |∫_{P_v} (f − f_θ) dH^m| ≤ θ H^m(P_v ∩ B_{R+1}(0)) = θ ω_m (R+1)^m (the isometry ι of step 2 carries L^m to H^m⌞P_v and B_{R+1}(0) ⊆ ℝ^m onto P_v ∩ B_{R+1}(0)). subproblems.title: A flat tangent measure gives density one and the cone condition (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(3))
subproblems.statement: Let m ≥ 1, μ a Borel measure on ℝ^{m+1}, y ∈ ℝ^{m+1} and v ∈ ℝ^{m+1} with |v| = 1. Assume μ(B̄_{r₀}(y)) < ∞ for some r₀ > 0, and r^{-m} ∫ f(r^{-1}(z − y)) dμ(z) → ∫_{(span{v})^⊥} f dH^m as r ↓ 0 for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ (H^m = μHE[m]). Then, as r ↓ 0, μ(B̄_r(y))/(ω_m r^m) → 1 and μ(B_r(y))/(ω_m r^m) → 1 in [0, ∞] (ω_m = unitBallVolume m), and for every α > 0, μ({z : α|z − y| ≤ |⟨z − y, v⟩|} ∩ B̄_r(y))/r^m → 0.

Source. Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(3) (chapter-03.txt lines 91–107), applied to the measure μ instead of H^n⌞M; it supplies the facts (5)–(6) used in the printed proof of 1.6 "⇐" and the density Θ^m(μ_E, x) = 1 of 4.3. Parent proof steps 4(12), 5, 6.

Notation. E := ℝ^{m+1}, P := (span{v})^⊥, H^m := μHE[m], ω_m := unitBallVolume m = L^m(B_1(0)) ∈ (0, ∞), I_r(f) := r^{-m} ∫ f(r^{-1}(z − y)) dμ(z), I(f) := ∫_P f dH^m. Hypothesis: I_r(f) → I(f) as r ↓ 0 for every continuous compactly supported f. Let r₀ be as in the hypothesis.

1. Plane balls. P has dimension m. A linear isometry ι : ℝ^m → P carries Lebesgue measure L^m to H^m⌞P (μHE[m] is isometry invariant and equals volume on ℝ^m) and ι^{-1}(P ∩ B̄_s(0)) = B̄_s(0), ι^{-1}(P ∩ B_s(0)) = B_s(0). Hence H^m(P ∩ B_s(0)) = H^m(P ∩ B̄_s(0)) = ω_m s^m for s ≥ 0 (spheres are L^m-null).

2. Ball densities. Fix 0 < ε < 1 and let f₊(w) := min(1, max(0, (1 + ε − |w|)/ε)) and f₋(w) := min(1, max(0, (1 − |w|)/ε)). They are continuous with compact support and 1_{B̄_{1−ε}} ≤ f₋ ≤ 1_{B_1} ≤ 1_{B̄_1} ≤ f₊ ≤ 1_{B̄_{1+ε}}. Since 1_{B̄_1}(r^{-1}(z − y)) = 1_{B̄_r(y)}(z) and similarly for open balls, for 0 < r ≤ r₀/2 (all integrands vanish outside B̄_{r₀}(y), where μ is finite)
 I_r(f₋) ≤ r^{-m} μ(B_r(y)) ≤ r^{-m} μ(B̄_r(y)) ≤ I_r(f₊).
 As r ↓ 0, I_r(f₊) → I(f₊) ≤ H^m(P ∩ B̄_{1+ε}(0)) = ω_m(1 + ε)^m and I_r(f₋) → I(f₋) ≥ H^m(P ∩ B̄_{1−ε}(0)) = ω_m(1 − ε)^m. So ω_m(1 − ε)^m ≤ liminf r^{-m} μ(B_r(y)) ≤ limsup r^{-m} μ(B̄_r(y)) ≤ ω_m(1 + ε)^m; letting ε ↓ 0, r^{-m} μ(B_r(y)) → ω_m and r^{-m} μ(B̄_r(y)) → ω_m. Dividing by ω_m ∈ (0, ∞): μ(B̄_r(y))/(ω_m r^m) → 1 and μ(B_r(y))/(ω_m r^m) → 1 in [0, ∞].

3. Cone. Let α > 0, K_α := {w : α|w| ≤ |⟨w, v⟩| and |w| ≤ 1} (compact), and for 0 < θ < 1 let f_θ(w) := max(0, 1 − dist(w, K_α)/θ): continuous, 0 ≤ f_θ ≤ 1, f_θ = 1 on K_α, and f_θ vanishes outside the closed θ-neighbourhood of K_α, which lies in B̄_{1+θ}(0); so f_θ has compact support. If α|z − y| ≤ |⟨z − y, v⟩| and |z − y| ≤ r then r^{-1}(z − y) ∈ K_α; hence for 0 < r ≤ r₀/2, r^{-m} μ({z : α|z − y| ≤ |⟨z − y, v⟩|} ∩ B̄_r(y)) ≤ I_r(f_θ) → I(f_θ). If w ∈ P and f_θ(w) > 0, pick k ∈ K_α with |w − k| < θ; since ⟨w, v⟩ = 0, α|k| ≤ |⟨k, v⟩| = |⟨k − w, v⟩| < θ, so |w| < θ(1 + 1/α). Thus I(f_θ) ≤ H^m(P ∩ B_{θ(1+1/α)}(0)) = ω_m θ^m (1 + 1/α)^m, and limsup_{r↓0} r^{-m} μ({z : α|z − y| ≤ |⟨z − y, v⟩|} ∩ B̄_r(y)) ≤ ω_m θ^m (1 + 1/α)^m for every θ ∈ (0, 1). Letting θ ↓ 0, the ratio μ({z : α|z − y| ≤ |⟨z − y, v⟩|} ∩ B̄_r(y))/r^m tends to 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: H^m(P ∩ B_s) = H^m(P ∩ B̄_s) = ω_m s^m for the m-plane P = v^⊥.
Sandwich 1_{B̄_1} between continuous f₋ ≤ f₊ to get density one for closed and open balls.
Test the cone with f_θ = (1 − dist(·,K_α)/θ)⁺; on P it lives in B_{θ(1+1/α)}, so the cone ratio → 0.

subproblems.title: A measure with flat tangent measures a.e. is carried by a countably m-rectifiable set (Simon Ch. 3, 1.6 ⇐)
subproblems.statement: Let m ≥ 1, let D ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} be open, μ a Borel measure on ℝ^{m+1} with μ(ℝ^{m+1} \ D) = 0 and μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ D, and ν : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m+1} Borel with |ν(y)| = 1 for every y. Assume that for μ-a.e. y and every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ, r^{-m} ∫ f(r^{-1}(z − y)) dμ(z) → ∫_{(span{ν(y)})^⊥} f dH^m as r ↓ 0 (H^m = μHE[m]). Then there is a Borel countably m-rectifiable set R ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} with μ(ℝ^{m+1} \ R) = 0.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Printed proof of Simon Ch. 3, 1.6 "⇐" (chapter-03.txt lines 145–270), with the measure μ in place of H^n⌞(M ∩ B_R(0)), codimension ℓ = 1, normal lines π_x = ℝν(x) and planes P_x = π_x^⊥; parent proof step 6. Departures (rigour only): Simon's appeal to 1.15 of Ch. 1 and to Egoroff's theorem in (4), (7)–(9) is replaced by explicit Borel sets G_k and inner regularity (measurability of the printed f_k, q_k is not addressed in print); the Lipschitz extension is McShane's scalar extension (Ch. 2, 1.2, chapter-02.txt line 33; Mathlib `LipschitzOnWith.extend_real`). Dependency: flat_tangent_density.

Notation. E := ℝ^{m+1}; G := {x ∈ D : the flat-tangent convergence holds at x with the plane (span{ν(x)})^⊥}, so μ(E \ G) = 0; for x ∈ E, a unit vector u and β ∈ (0, 1), X_β(u, x) := {z : β|z − x| ≤ |⟨z − x, u⟩|} (a closed cone around the normal line x + ℝu); ω_m := unitBallVolume m.

0. Reduction. Claim (★): for every open U with compact closure Ū ⊆ D there is a closed countably m-rectifiable Γ ⊆ E with μ(U \ Γ) ≤ ½ μ(U). Granting (★): choose countably many open balls W_l with W̄_l ⊆ D and ⋃_l W_l = D. For fixed l let U_0 := W_l and U_{i+1} := U_i \ Γ_{l,i}, where Γ_{l,i} is given by (★) for U_i (U_{i+1} is open and Ū_{i+1} ⊆ W̄_l). Then μ(U_i) ≤ 2^{-i} μ(W_l) and μ(W_l) ≤ μ(W̄_l) < ∞, so μ(W_l \ ⋃_i Γ_{l,i}) = 0. R := ⋃_{l,i} Γ_{l,i} is Borel (a countable union of closed sets) and countably m-rectifiable (SimonGMT `countablyRectifiable_iUnion`), and μ(E \ R) ≤ μ(E \ D) + Σ_l μ(W_l \ R) = 0.

1. Localization. Fix U as in (★) and let λ := μ⌞U, a finite Borel measure; if λ(E) = 0 take Γ := ∅. Let x ∈ U ∩ G. If f is continuous with support in B_S(0) and 0 < r < dist(x, E \ U)/S, then f(r^{-1}(z − x)) ≠ 0 implies z ∈ U, so ∫ f(r^{-1}(z − x)) dλ = ∫ f(r^{-1}(z − x)) dμ. Hence λ satisfies the flat-tangent hypothesis at x with the plane (span{ν(x)})^⊥, and λ(B̄_1(x)) < ∞. By flat_tangent_density (with v := ν(x), α := 1/4), as ρ ↓ 0:
 (5) λ(B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_m ρ^m) → 1,  (6) λ(X_{1/4}(ν(x), x) ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/ρ^m → 0.

2. Uniformization (replaces printed (4), (7)–(9)). Let ε := 1/(2(1 + 16^m)). For k ≥ 1 let G_k be the set of x ∈ U such that for every rational q ∈ (0, 1/k): λ(B̄_q(x)) ≥ (1 − ε) ω_m q^m and λ(X_{1/4}(ν(x), x) ∩ B̄_q(x)) ≤ ε ω_m q^m.
 (a) G_k is Borel: x ↦ λ(B̄_q(x)) is upper semicontinuous; (x, u) ↦ λ({z : ¼|z − x| ≤ |⟨z − x, u⟩|, |z − x| ≤ q}) is upper semicontinuous on E × E, because the set of (x, u, z) satisfying these closed conditions is closed and λ is finite (reverse Fatou); its composition with the Borel map x ↦ (x, ν(x)) is Borel. G_k is U intersected with countably many Borel sets.
 (b) For x ∈ G_k both inequalities hold for every real ρ ∈ (0, 1/k): approximate ρ from below by rationals for the first (monotonicity in the radius), and from above by rationals q ↓ ρ with q < 1/k for the second (continuity from above of the finite measure λ along the decreasing closed sets).
 (c) G_k ⊆ G_{k+1}, and U ∩ G ⊆ ⋃_k G_k by (5)–(6) (ω_m > 0). As λ(U \ G) = 0, continuity from below gives k with λ(U \ G_k) ≤ ¼ λ(U); by inner regularity of the finite Borel measure λ on E there is a compact E₀ ⊆ G_k with λ(G_k \ E₀) ≤ ¼ λ(U). Thus λ(U \ E₀) ≤ ½ λ(U). Put δ := 1/k.

3. Reference directions (printed choice of π_1, …, π_N). By compactness of the unit sphere choose unit vectors v_1, …, v_N such that every unit vector lies within distance 1/16 of some v_j. Let E_j := {x ∈ E₀ : |ν(x) − v_j| < 1/16}; then E₀ = ⋃_j E_j.

4. Cone exclusion (printed (10)). Claim: if x ∈ E_j, x′ ∈ E₀ and 0 < |x′ − x| < δ/2, then |⟨x′ − x, v_j⟩| < ½|x′ − x|. Suppose not; let ρ := |x′ − x| and w := x′ − x, so |⟨w, v_j⟩| ≥ ρ/2. Then |⟨w, ν(x)⟩| ≥ |⟨w, v_j⟩| − ρ|ν(x) − v_j| ≥ ρ/2 − ρ/16 = 7ρ/16. For z ∈ B̄_{ρ/8}(x′): |⟨z − x, ν(x)⟩| ≥ 7ρ/16 − ρ/8 = 5ρ/16 ≥ ¼·(9ρ/8) ≥ ¼|z − x|, and |z − x| ≤ 9ρ/8 < 2ρ. So B̄_{ρ/8}(x′) ⊆ X_{1/4}(ν(x), x) ∩ B̄_{2ρ}(x). As x′ ∈ G_k and ρ/8 < δ, λ(B̄_{ρ/8}(x′)) ≥ (1 − ε) ω_m (ρ/8)^m; as x ∈ G_k and 2ρ < δ, λ(X_{1/4}(ν(x), x) ∩ B̄_{2ρ}(x)) ≤ ε ω_m (2ρ)^m. Hence (1 − ε) 8^{-m} ≤ ε 2^m, i.e. 1 − ε ≤ 16^m ε, contradicting ε = 1/(2(1 + 16^m)).

5. Lipschitz graphs (printed "E_j ∩ B_{δ/4}(x₀) ⊆ Q^T(graph f)"). Fix j and x₀ ∈ E₀, and let S := E_j ∩ B_{δ/4}(x₀). Let p_j be the orthogonal projection onto v_j^⊥ and t_j(x) := ⟨x, v_j⟩. For distinct x, x′ ∈ S we have |x − x′| < δ/2, so step 4 gives |t_j(x′) − t_j(x)| < ½|x′ − x| ≤ ½(|p_j(x′) − p_j(x)| + |t_j(x′) − t_j(x)|), whence |t_j(x′) − t_j(x)| < |p_j(x′) − p_j(x)|. Thus p_j is injective on S and τ := t_j ∘ (p_j|_S)^{-1} is 1-Lipschitz on p_j(S) ⊆ v_j^⊥; McShane's extension gives a 1-Lipschitz τ̃ : v_j^⊥ → ℝ extending τ. With a linear isometry ι_j : ℝ^m → v_j^⊥ (dim v_j^⊥ = m), F_{j,x₀}(w) := ι_j(w) + τ̃(ι_j(w)) v_j is a Lipschitz map ℝ^m → E whose range Γ_{j,x₀} = {z : τ̃(p_j(z)) = t_j(z)} is closed, and S ⊆ Γ_{j,x₀} because each x ∈ S equals p_j(x) + τ̃(p_j(x)) v_j.

6. Finite cover. E₀ is compact, so E₀ ⊆ ⋃_{l ≤ L} B_{δ/4}(x₀^l) for some x₀^l ∈ E₀. Hence E₀ = ⋃_{j,l} (E_j ∩ B_{δ/4}(x₀^l)) ⊆ Γ := ⋃_{j,l} Γ_{j,x₀^l}, a finite union of closed ranges of Lipschitz maps ℝ^m → E; Γ is closed and countably m-rectifiable (SimonGMT `countablyRectifiable_range`, `countablyRectifiable_iUnion`). Finally μ(U \ Γ) = λ(U \ Γ) ≤ λ(U \ E₀) ≤ ½ λ(U) = ½ μ(U), which proves (★). ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to halving: each open U ⋐ D contains a closed rectifiable Γ with μ(U∖Γ) ≤ ½μ(U); iterate and take countable unions.
On U ∩ G the localized measure μ⌞U has density one and a vanishing cone ratio (flat_tangent_density).
Borel uniformization sets G_k and inner regularity give a compact E₀ with uniform density/cone bounds and μ(U∖E₀) ≤ ½μ(U).
Cone exclusion (printed (10)) with finitely many reference directions v_j.
Points of E_j ∩ B_{δ/4}(x₀) lie on a 1-Lipschitz graph over v_j^⊥ (McShane extension).
Finitely many Lipschitz graphs cover E₀.

subproblems.title: Identification μ = H^m⌞B with approximate tangent planes ν^⊥, given rectifiable density one (Simon 4.3 first part)
subproblems.statement: Let m ≥ 1, let D ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} be open, μ a Borel measure on ℝ^{m+1} with μ(ℝ^{m+1} \ D) = 0 and μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ D, and ν : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m+1} Borel with |ν(y)| = 1 for every y. Assume that for μ-a.e. y and every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ, r^{-m} ∫ f(r^{-1}(z − y)) dμ(z) → ∫_{(span{ν(y)})^⊥} f dH^m as r ↓ 0 (H^m = μHE[m]). Assume also (RD): for every Borel countably m-rectifiable S ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} with H^m(S) < ∞, H^m(S ∩ B_t(w))/(ω_m t^m) → 1 as t ↓ 0 for H^m-a.e. w ∈ S (ω_m = unitBallVolume m). Then there is a Borel, countably m-rectifiable B ⊆ D with μ = H^m⌞B (as measures) such that for H^m-a.e. y ∈ B the approximate tangent space of B at y (Simon Ch. 3, 1.4) is (span{ν(y)})^⊥.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Expansion of the printed first sentence of the proof of Simon Ch. 3, 4.3 ("By 1.6 and 3.6 of Ch. 1, the first part of the theorem follows from 4.3(†)", chapter-03.txt line 604), exactly as in parent proof steps 5, 7 and 8: comparison of μ with H^m (Ch. 1, 3.2–3.4, chapter-01.txt lines 578–640), Radon–Nikodym differentiation (Ch. 1, 3.23–3.24, lines 1063–1180; Mathlib `Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_rnDeriv`), the rectifiable density theorem (hypothesis (RD); in the parent it is supplied by the sibling rectifiable_density_one, `Submission.codim1_rdo_rectifiable_ae_density_one` with P := m + 1, n := m), and Definition 1.4 of Ch. 3 (chapter-03.txt lines 80–90). Dependencies: flat_tangent_density, rectifiable_criterion.

Notation. E := ℝ^{m+1}; H^m := μHE[m] = κ_m·μH[m] for a constant κ_m ∈ (0, ∞) (definition of μHE); ω_m := unitBallVolume m; P_y := (span{ν(y)})^⊥; G := {y ∈ D : the flat-tangent convergence holds at y}, so μ(E \ G) = 0.

1. Density of μ. For y ∈ G some B̄_{r₀}(y) ⊆ D (D open) has finite μ-measure, so flat_tangent_density gives μ(B̄_r(y))/(ω_m r^m) → 1 and μ(B_r(y))/(ω_m r^m) → 1 as r ↓ 0.

2. Carrier. rectifiable_criterion gives a Borel countably m-rectifiable R with μ(E \ R) = 0. Let N := toMeasurable μ (E \ G) (Borel, N ⊇ E \ G, μ(N) = 0) and B := (D ∩ R) \ N. Then B is Borel, B ⊆ D, B ⊆ R ∩ G, B is countably m-rectifiable (`CountablyRectifiable.mono`), and μ(E \ B) ≤ μ(E \ D) + μ(E \ R) + μ(N) = 0. Let λ := μHE[m].restrict B.

3. Local finiteness of λ (comparison of Ch. 1, 3.3 type). Claim: H^m(B ∩ V) ≤ c_m μ(V) for every open V with V̄ compact ⊆ D, where c_m := 2·10^m κ_m/ω_m. Fix θ > 0. Every x ∈ B ∩ V lies in G, so by step 1 there are arbitrarily small r ∈ (0, θ/10) with B̄_r(x) ⊆ V and μ(B̄_r(x)) ≥ ½ ω_m r^m. By the 5r-covering lemma (Ch. 1, 3.4; Mathlib `Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement_closedBall`) there is a disjoint subfamily B̄_{r_i}(x_i), countable because each member has positive μ-measure and μ(V) < ∞, with B ∩ V ⊆ ⋃_i B̄_{5r_i}(x_i). As diam B̄_{5r_i}(x_i) ≤ 10 r_i < θ, the θ-approximation of μH[m] satisfies μH[m]_θ(B ∩ V) ≤ Σ_i (10 r_i)^m ≤ (2·10^m/ω_m) Σ_i μ(B̄_{r_i}(x_i)) ≤ (2·10^m/ω_m) μ(V).
